title: Fixing Kafka Hot-Partition Skew
prompt: A multi-tenant analytics pipeline produces 25,000 events/sec into a 32-partition Kafka topic keyed by tenant_id. One enterprise tenant ('acme-corp') generates 68% of all traffic (17,000 events/sec, ~17 MB/s). Because Murmur2(tenant_id) % 32 deterministically maps 'acme-corp' to partition 14, partition 14 receives 17,000 msg/s while the other 31 partitions average 258 msg/s each. Consumer pod #14 is 100% CPU-saturated with 4.5M lag, broker #3 disk I/O is pinned at 98%, and the other 31 consumer threads sit at 3% CPU. Redesign the partitioning and consumer aggregation strategy to balance load across partitions without breaking per-tenant analytics.

spark.summary: When whale tenant acme-corp (68% of 25k events/sec) pins partition 14 at 17,000 msg/s while 31 partitions sit idle, adaptive key salting (acme-corp#0..15) + two-stage tumbling aggregation balances all 32 partitions under 2x cluster average.

explanation.foundation: Production Kafka pipelines balance load without losing ordering or accuracy:
explanation.core:

- **Zero-Loss Migration**: Deploy Stage 2 / dual-key consumers first, then flip producer salting.
